You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e58decc9c51eb61697aba35ba8eda33f4b80552d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2018 02:10:27 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] nfp: fix error return code in nfp_pci_probe()

Fix to return error code -EINVAL instead of 0 when num_vfs above
limit_vfs, as done elsewhere in this function.

Fixes: 0dc786219186 ("nfp: handle SR-IOV already enabled when driver is probing")
Signed-off-by: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Acked-by: Jakub Kicinski <jakub.kicinski@netronome.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/nfp_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/nfp_main.c
index c5b91040b12e..cc570bb6563c 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/nfp_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/nfp_main.c
@@ -518,6 +518,7 @@ static int nfp_pci_probe(struct pci_dev *pdev,
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev,
 			"Error: %d VFs already enabled, but loaded FW can only support %d\n",
 			pf->num_vfs, pf->limit_vfs);
+		err = -EINVAL;
 		goto err_fw_unload;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File Modified: `nfp_main.c`**
- A line was added to set the error code to `-EINVAL` when the number of virtual functions (`num_vfs`) exceeds the limit (`limit_vfs`). This change occurs within the `nfp_pci_probe` function, specifically after an error message is logged. The previous behavior returned `0` in this scenario, which was incorrect.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug identified in the previous implementation of the `nfp_pci_probe` function, where an incorrect error code was returned when the number of virtual functions exceeded the supported limit. The change ensures consistency with the error handling logic used elsewhere in the function, thereby improving the robustness of the driver. The patch is linked to a specific commit that introduced the issue, indicating that this fix is a corrective measure for that earlier change.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
pf->num_vfs = pci_num_vf(pdev);
if (pf->num_vfs > pf->limit_vfs) {
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code checks if the number of virtual functions (`num_vfs`) exceeds the maximum allowed (`limit_vfs`), but it incorrectly returns `0` (indicating success) instead of an appropriate error code when this condition is met. This misleading behavior can lead to the driver operating under the false assumption that the operation was successful.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
err = -EINVAL;
goto err_fw_unload;
```
Reason:
The fix involves setting the error code to `-EINVAL` when the number of virtual functions exceeds the limit. This change ensures that the function correctly indicates an error condition, allowing the caller to handle the situation appropriately and preventing the driver from proceeding as if the operation was successful.
